gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: They've postponed ___ the new bridge until spring.
We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.

gaps.sentence: I've always wanted ___ how to sail.
He was the first climber ___ the summit without oxygen.
gaps.explanation: After 'the first/last/only + noun' a to-infinitive follows.

gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ something to eat at the motorway services.
gaps.explanation: 'Stopped to get' = paused for the purpose; 'stopped getting' would mean quit eating.
bother + -ing (or to-infinitive): don't bother going. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: It's no use ___ to start the engine — the battery is completely flat.
gaps.explanation: 'It's no use' is followed by a gerund.
